## Engine and packages
- Unity **6000.3.6f1**, **URP 17.3.0** (quality-tiered pipeline assets in `Assets/Settings/`, main
  `Assets/RenderPipeline/TheLastEngineerHQ.asset`), Volumetric Fog (`com.cqf.urpvolumetricfog`, git).
- Input System 1.18 (Active Input Handling = **Both**; new code uses only the Input System).
- Cinemachine 3.1.6, Timeline 1.8.10, VFX Graph 17.3.0, ProBuilder 6.0.8, FBX Exporter.
- **PrimeTween** (local tgz under `Assets/Plugins/PrimeTween`) for all tweens. `DOTWEEN` appears in
  scripting defines but DOTween is not in the project — TODO: confirm it's a leftover.
- UI: **UGUI + TextMesh Pro** at runtime; UI Toolkit only in editor tools (Prefab Painter).
- QuickOutline (Asset Store, `Assets/Art/Store Meshes/QuickOutline`) for node outlines.
- No DI container, no Addressables.

## Runtime systems and boundaries
All gameplay is in `Assembly-CSharp` (no asmdefs), so boundaries are by convention, not compiler.
- **Player** — `PlayerController` (hub MonoBehaviour) creates plain-class `PlayerModel` (movement,
  dash, teleport via `CharacterController`) and `PlayerView` (anim, particles, SFX), the
  `PlayerStateMachine` and `InteractableHandler`. Components: `InputHandler` (input → C# events),
  `PlayerNodeHandler` (node in hand), `GlitchTransferHandler` (Set/Take), `PlayerInteractionDetector`
  (sole interactable registry: trigger + per-frame revalidation + line of sight).
- **Glitch** — `GlitchComponent` holds the level (truth), `GlitchTransferManager` (static) is the only
  mutator, `GlitchPalette` the only color source; `Glitcheable` reconciles its FSM with the level.
- **Puzzle elements** — `NodeController`, `Connection`, `DoorController`, `PressurePlate`/`PressuredDoor`,
  `LaserController` (MVC), `PlatformController` (+ FSM), `PlatformTeleport`.
- **Inspection** (`Assets/Inspection System/`) — separate camera + canvas; switches the player to the `UI` action map.
- **Cinematics** — `CinematicManager` drives camera priorities and waypoint navigation of the player.
- **Services** — `InputManager`, `LevelLoader`, `SFXManager`, `UIButtonsManager`, `GlitchDeathController`.

## Communication
- **C# events** (`Action` / `event Action`), subscribed/unsubscribed symmetrically
  (`OnEnable/OnDisable` or `Start/OnDestroy`). Examples: `Connection.OnNodeConnected`,
  `IActivationSource.OnActivationChanged`, `GlitchComponent.OnGlitchStateChanged`,
  `GlitchStateMachine.OnStateChanged`, `PlayerController.OnDied/OnRespawned`,
  `LevelLoader.OnLoading`, `CinematicManager.OnRequestEnterCinematicState`.
- **UnityEvents** only for inspector wiring (laser receptors, `ShaderFiller`, `ResetPressurePlate`).
- **Interfaces** as contracts between systems: `IInteractable`, `IProximityListener`,
  `IActivationSource`, `IConnectable`, `IMovablePassenger`, `ILaserReceptor`, `IObstructionChecker`, `IScreen`.
- **Singletons** (`public static X Instance` set in `Awake`): `PlayerController`, `PlayerNodeHandler`,
  `InputManager`, `LevelLoader` (`DontDestroyOnLoad`), `CinematicManager`, `ScreenManager`,
  `UIButtonsManager`, `SFXManager`, `PlatesActivator`, `InspectionSystem`, `InspectorController`,
  `CorruptionRemover`, `ScannerController`, `GamepadCursor`, `GlitchDeathController`, `FloorDitherManager` (prototype).
- **ScriptableObject defaults via Resources**: `GlitchPalette.Default`, `LaserData.Default`.

## Patterns in use
| Pattern | Where | Problem it solves |
|---|---|---|
| MVC (Controller MonoBehaviour + plain Model/View made in `Awake`) | Player, Node, Laser (`LaserView` is a MonoBehaviour) | Separate logic from visuals/feedback |
| State machine (cached state instances, `ToX()`/`TransitionToX()`, `Tick` from owner `Update`) | `PlayerStateMachine`, `PlatformStateMachine`, `GlitchStateMachine` | Mode-dependent behavior |
| Observer (C# events) | everywhere | Decouple puzzle elements and views |
| Singleton | services and managers above | Global access (team intent per root README is to avoid it in puzzles, but it's the actual pattern) |
| Static service | `GlitchTransferManager` | Single atomic mutator of glitch charge |
| Stack of screens | `ScreenManager` + `IScreen` | Alternative pause/menu flow |

Legacy code coexists with current versions — check which one the `BUILD SCENES` prefabs use before
extending: `Laser`/`AntiCorruptionLaser` vs `LaserController`; `PauseMenu` (legacy `Input`) vs
`PauseGameController` (current) vs `ScreenManager`; root `PreassurePlate` vs `Gameplay/Pressure Plate/PressurePlate`;
`GlitcheableDetector` (unused).

## Startup and scene flow
- No bootstrap scene. Build index 0 is the main menu; each level scene contains its own Player,
  `InputManager` and `LevelLoader`, so levels can be played directly in the Editor.
- `LevelLoader.SetScene(name)`: fade → `OnLoading` (player input off) → `LoadSceneAsync` with
  `allowSceneActivation = false` while the elevator animation plays (min `minLoadingDuration`) → fade.
  Used by `MainMenu`, `PauseGameController`, `GoToMenu`.
- `SceneTransition` (shader-based) and `LevelSelector` (number keys to checkpoints) are debug utilities.

## Save / load
- No persistence found: no `PlayerPrefs`, file I/O or JSON saving in code. A scene
  `TEST LEVELS/Juli/TEST SaveLoad Data.unity` exists — TODO: save system status.
- Checkpoints are runtime-only (`PlayerController` checkpoint position).

## Runtime tests
- None. There are no test assemblies (`*.asmdef` with test references) and the Test Framework is
  only present via `com.unity.feature.development`. `/run-tests` has nothing to run until a test
  asmdef exists — and a test asmdef can't reference `Assembly-CSharp`, so testing gameplay code
  needs an asmdef for it first. TODO: decide a test setup.
